summary: The Fairbanks court opened three criminal cases that appeared in its public database during Tuesday, among them a Class C felony assault charge filed on an offense date of the same day. Neither the Alaska State Troopers dispatch nor the Fairbanks police bulletin had reported anything in the Fairbanks area for Tuesday at the time of reading. A charging document was filed in the household assault arrest troopers reported late on Monday, and the court entered a Governor's Warrant of Arrest in a Fort Wainwright extradition case. The 42 Fairbanks filings counted below are the weekly charges report's own count for Nov. 17 to Nov. 23; the court also holds at least one case filed inside that window which the report does not list, 4FA-26-02342CR, filed Nov. 19.

entries.title: Felony assault charge: Jeremiah Alexander
body: Jeremiah Alexander is charged with assault in the third degree - causing fear of injury with a weapon - a Class C felony, punishable by up to five years. Fairbanks, offense date Nov. 24; the charge is recorded in the Alaska Court System case record.
The charge stands on a complaint rather than an indictment, and the court does not record it as domestic violence related.
Case 4FA-26-02340CR, before Judge Earl A. Peterson. Arraignment was held Nov. 24; preliminary hearings are set for Dec. 3 and Dec. 14.

entries.title: Assault arrest: Julianna Nicholson
body: Julianna Nicholson, 29, of Fairbanks was arrested on charges of assault in the fourth degree, violating conditions of release, and an outstanding warrant. Assault in the fourth degree is recklessly injuring another person. Fairbanks, Nov. 23; Alaska State Troopers.
Troopers say they responded to a residence in Fairbanks for a report of a disturbance and determined that Nicholson had assaulted a household member and had also violated her conditions of release.

A charging document was filed on Nov. 24 in case 4FA-26-02341CR: one count of assault in the fourth degree, a Class A misdemeanor the court records as domestic violence related, and one count of violating conditions of release on a misdemeanor, a Class B misdemeanor. Arraignment was held Nov. 24; a pre-trial conference is set for Jan. 14, 2027 and trial week for Jan. 25, 2027.

The warrant was issued on Nov. 19 by the Fairbanks court in case 4FA-26-01389CR, a separate open case in which Nicholson is charged with assault in the fourth degree, a Class A misdemeanor the court records as domestic violence related. Bail on the warrant was set at a $250 performance bond and a $500 unsecured appearance bond.

entries.title: Governor's Warrant of Arrest entered in Fort Wainwright extradition case: Brenden James Clarke
body: The Fairbanks court entered a Governor's Warrant of Arrest and a fugitive-from-justice temporary order on Nov. 24 in the case of Brenden James Clarke. The case is recorded as an arrest prior to requisition, fugitive from justice, offense location Fort Wainwright.
No charge class is recorded on the file, and the charges that another state may be pursuing are not part of this record.
Case 4FA-26-01857CR, before Judge Ben A. Seekins; next hearing Dec. 15.

entries.title: Felony drug warrant arrest: Scott Kranenburg
body: Scott Richard Kranenburg was arrested on a felony warrant in case 3GL-26-00092CR, in which he is charged with misconduct involving a controlled substance in the third degree - manufacturing or delivering a controlled substance - a Class B felony, punishable by up to 10 years. A second count, endangering the welfare of a child in the second degree, is recorded by the court as a non-criminal violation.

Troopers say they contacted him at the Tok Trooper Post on Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. and arrested him on the warrant. He was remanded to the Fairbanks Correctional Center on $1,000 bail, which the court record shows as posted.

The court records the offense at Glennallen on Feb. 22. The case was opened at the Glennallen court on Nov. 13 and arraignment is set for Dec. 1. Tok and Glennallen are outside the Fairbanks area this report covers; the arrest appears here because he was held at the Fairbanks jail.

entries.title: Assault and child-present charges: Emeline Janice Gallahorn
body: Emeline Janice Gallahorn is charged with assault in the fourth degree - recklessly injuring another person - and with six counts of assault when a child is present, all seven Class A misdemeanors. The court records all seven counts as domestic violence related.
Fairbanks, offense date Nov. 19. Case 4FA-26-02319CR, before Judge Maria P. Bahr. Arraignment was held Nov. 20 and the court entered a writ of assistance in a domestic violence matter the same day.
A pre-trial conference is set for Jan. 14, 2027 and trial week for Jan. 25, 2027. Nothing beyond the court record is reported here.

entries.title: Driving with a revoked license: Akeil Natna Peebles
body: Akeil Natna Peebles is charged with driving while his license was canceled, revoked or suspended, with a previous conviction - a Class A misdemeanor. Fairbanks, offense date Nov. 16.
Case 4FA-26-02342CR, filed Nov. 19 before Judge Ben A. Seekins. The charge was brought by the prosecutor on an Information rather than on a police complaint, and no hearing is set on the file.

entries.title: Five Fairbanks cases opened in one week with no charging document filed
body: Five of the 42 criminal cases opened at the Fairbanks court between Nov. 17 and Nov. 23 carry a single entry recording a charging document as pending or not filed, and no charge or degree of offense. No charge has been brought in any of them.

4FA-26-02307CR, State of Alaska vs. Shay Pitka, offense date Nov. 18. 4FA-26-02316CR, State of Alaska vs. Katrina Albert, Nov. 19. 4FA-26-02317CR, State of Alaska vs. Arlo Charles Leroy Smoke, Nov. 19. 4FA-26-02320CR, State of Alaska vs. Felipe Soto Gomez, Nov. 20. 4FA-26-02337CR, State of Alaska vs. Shane Trevor O'Brien, Nov. 22.

The court's weekly disposed-cases report shows three of the five - the Pitka, Albert and Smoke cases - already closed, with no charge ever filed. In the O'Brien case the court entered an order and conditions of release on Nov. 24, and arraignment is set for Nov. 27; still no charge is recorded.
